meaning:
ἄδικος, -ον
(δίκη), [in LXX for שׁקר, עול, etc. ;]
1. unjust: Rom.3:5, Heb.6:10.
2. unrighteous, wicked: Luk.16:11 18:11, Act.24:15, 1Co.6:1,9 1Pe.3:18; opposite to δίκαιος, Mat.5:45; to εὐσεβής, 2Pe.2:9; to πιστός, Luk.16:10 (Cremer, 200).
† (AS)

elsewhere.note: that you may be children of your Father who is in heaven. For he makes his sun to rise on the evil and the good, and sends rain on the just and the unjust.
He who is faithful in a very little is faithful also in much. He who is dishonest in a very little is also dishonest in much.
having hope toward God, which these also themselves look for, that there will be a resurrection of the dead, both of the just and unjust.
But if our unrighteousness commends the righteousness of God, what will we say? Is God unrighteous who inflicts wrath? I speak like men do.
Dare any of you, having a matter against his neighbor, go to law before the unrighteous, and not before the saints?
For God is not unrighteous, so as to forget your work and the labor of love which you showed toward his name, in that you served the saints, and still do serve…
Because Christ also suffered for sins once, the righteous for the unrighteous, that he might bring you to God, being put to death in the flesh, but made alive…
the Lord knows how to deliver the godly out of temptation and to keep the unrighteous under punishment for the day of judgment,
